headline: Candidate: making checked the default policy for the Jev provider. On 4 checked cases x 2 repetitions, arm B (Haiku first, one Sonnet retry on a failed check) passed 8/8, the same as arm A (all Sonnet) at 8/8. Price-weighted cost was $0.244 against $0.869 (-72%). Jev was called 0 times on these checked tasks. Haiku failed d5-deps on its first try in both repetitions; the cascade caught both. Sample size is small, so Gate B should decide.

arms.name: Every case agent on Sonnet 5.5, no router, no cascade
route.mjs default (policy checked, provider jev) per exact prompt, with one cascade retry (--escalate-from) on a failed check
arms.model: router output: haiku (all 4 cases), sonnet on cascade retry (d5-deps only)
arms.engineVersion: router.mjs loadConfig default policy checked for provider jev

evaluation.datasetVersion: bench/tasks d5-deps, f1-paginate, d3-maplimit, r1-rename (agents get files/ only; check.mjs run by us)
evaluation.tokenScope: cost is price-weighted from each case agent's subagent transcript (pricing.mjs; input, output, cache read and cache write). Per-case tokens are summed from each agent's transcript (input = input + cache read + cache write; output = output), deduplicated by message id. B's cascade retry tokens are in its case total. Cost and tokens use the same transcripts.
deviations: Track E: P1 is N/A (existing tool). Phases P2 and P3 were run in this control session, not in fresh phase sessions with capsules (no phases[] rows). The router change (P2) is small and was made and tested here; the live arms were run by the control session with the case-agent pattern from design.md.
Arm A was not checked with subagent_usage.mjs --forbid in this round, so the claim that arm A never used the tool rests on the arm definition only (no router call).

Offline gate passed before spend: recorded replay gives checked+jev 6/6 pass, cost 0.134 of opus (jev+gate+sc: 6/6, 0.606). The idea brief's 0.235 was from before route-jev.json was refreshed with live Jev; the current figure is 0.134 (evidence/offline-score.json).

Frozen rule applied as written: B's pass rate counts after the cascade (8/8 vs 8/8). B's first-try pass rate was 6/8 (d5-deps failed twice on Haiku) against A's 8/8 first try. The cascade is part of B by design, but a Gate B reader should weigh the first-try number.

Two cascade retries (d5-deps, rep1 and rep2) are included in B's cost and tokens: $0.1026 and $0.1052 at Sonnet price. Without them B's cost would be $0.0361 for the first tries alone, but that would not be a valid pass rate.
Routing calls: 8 route.mjs calls for arm B, 0 Jev provider calls (checked tasks use the rule tier). The orchestrator's own tokens are not in either arm's cost; they do not change the sign.
Four checked cases only, with a check and no hard verb. Unchecked tasks (where Jev still runs under checked) were not tested live, so the Jev path itself has no live evidence in this round.
Not in scope and not changed: the consistency() rule (unstable votes go to the highest tier) and the rule tier for design-kind bench tasks (checked gives them haiku).

phases.phase: Control + case agents (one session, not split)
